title: How much of the chikki is each broken piece?
description: A chikki of 24 equal squares breaks into a small piece and a bigger L-shaped piece. Cutting the whole chikki into equal pieces the size of the small one names both pieces. Keeko's doubt, that each piece is one half because there are two pieces, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: a piece is named by how many equal copies of it fill the whole. Watch for students who say each piece is one half just because the chikki broke into two pieces.

source: The picture shows a whole chikki. A picture of the chikki broken into 2 pieces is shown below. How much of the original chikki is each piece?
video_script.why: The child names a piece of a whole by how many equal copies of it fill the whole, and then measures the bigger piece in that unit.
video_script.substitution: Ask how many copies of the small piece fill the whole chikki, then count how many small pieces fit in the bigger piece.
video_script.anchor: A whole chikki of 24 equal small squares, 6 across and 4 down, broken into a small piece and a bigger L-shaped piece
video_script.wrong_answer: each piece is one half because the chikki broke into two pieces
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says each piece is one half because the chikki broke into two pieces. The small piece fits on the bigger piece three times, so the two pieces are not equal and the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The small piece is one fourth of the chikki

final_answer.value: small piece 1/4 chikki; bigger piece 3/4 chikki
final_answer.spoken: the small piece is one fourth of the chikki and the bigger piece is three fourths of the chikki

video_script.fraction_reading: one fourth, three fourths, one half
never_show: 1/2 as the size of either piece
maths_rules: whole chikki: 6 squares across, 4 down, 6 x 4 = 24 equal small squares
small piece: 3 across, 2 down, 3 x 2 = 6 squares
cut across the middle and down the middle: 4 equal pieces of 3 by 2 squares, so 4 copies of the small piece fill the whole and the small piece is 1/4
bigger L-shaped piece: 24 - 6 = 18 squares = 3 small pieces, so 3 x 1/4 = 3/4
check: 6 + 18 = 24 squares, the whole chikki, and 1/4 + 3/4 = 1
slip: two pieces does not make each piece 1/2; a half needs two equal pieces
video_script.design: One idea: a piece is one fourth when four copies of it fill the whole. Assumes shares of a roti into equal parts. Wrong idea: two pieces means halves. The whole chikki stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks each piece is one half because the chikki broke into two pieces.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the small piece fits on the bigger piece three times, so the two pieces are not equal.
<bookmark mark='equal'/>A half needs two equal pieces. Two pieces alone do not make halves.
